projects.title: Shop-wide AI rules audit for Etsy sellers
projects.pitch: For Etsy sellers with dozens or hundreds of existing listings: drop in the listings CSV you export from Shop Manager and get a prioritised, per-listing to-do list against Etsy's 22 October 2026 AI rules (unedited real photo, finished-result photo for patterns and recipes, AI disclosure, no AI-written instructions, no bot-made duplicates). Everything runs locally in the browser; no Etsy login or A…

decision.reason: Spec written; waiting for the review.

projects.trigger: Etsy announced stricter AI rules: at least one unedited photo of the real item for most listings, AI-generated patterns, recipes and instructions banned, bot-generated listings banned, and existing l…
projects.window: About 1 to 3 months. Etsy says removals will expand over the coming months and that it plans to extend its AI-image warnings to existing listings; per-listing compliance scanners (iscompliant.app, In…

reasons: it was not approved to be built

votes.rationale: The trigger is 13 days old, covered by Retail Dive, eMarketer, Digital Commerce 360 and seller-news sites, with existing listings explicitly required to change and no audit tool from Etsy yet. Existing scanners work per listing on general policy text, so the shop-wide audit for the AI rules is open; but those scanners or Etsy itself can close the gap quickly. The need is mostly one-off, which caps revenue and long-term potential.
concerns: Etsy ships its announced warnings for existing listings and the need shrinks
A per-listing scanner (iscompliant.app, InsightAgent) adds the AI rules and bulk mode within weeks
The tool cannot prove a photo is unedited; if sellers expect detection rather than a checklist, they will be disappointed
The listings CSV may lack a physical-or-digital flag, so classification is heuristic; the column names are unverified until tested on a real export

warnings: Do not change a prompt or a threshold because of one week or fewer than the cases shown: the numbers move with luck.
Change one thing at a time and compare the same indicator over the weeks before and after (the "versions" list marks each change).
A rating that predicts demand-test clicks may still not predict search traffic or revenue; these are different outcomes.

factors.description: rides a fresh trigger (a law, a release, a trend) and shipped first
built with or around a community; users contribute or talk about it
the output is shareable or embeddable and brings new users (links, cards, badges, scores)
lives inside an existing platform or workflow (extension, plugin, bot, API)
the visitor gets a useful result within seconds, with no setup
usable without an account; registration comes later, to save or to pay
does one job extremely well instead of being a suite
unique, curated or fresher data than the alternatives
clearly better UX and clarity than the category
privacy-first or local processing, or honesty, as a visible difference
a reason to come back (streaks, alerts, a daily puzzle, saved work)
games: short sessions, a simple core loop, instant restart, a shareable score

learning.insights: ## Calibration Too early. The portfolio has 1 idea (scouted, rated by 1 agent, composite 2.95) and **0 outcomes**. I cannot say which agent's ratings predict best. Revisit once about 5 shipped products have 4+ weeks of Search Console data. ## What works (only 1 site has numbers: n=1, so a correlation and not a cause) The one site with traction is a German-language programmatic directory of public procurement notices. Over 28 days it had about 286 clicks and 12.1k impressions, average position 15.7, and it is roughly 6 weeks old (age inferred). - Clicks come from **thousands of long-tail detail pages** (one notice per page) ranking in positions 3 to 5 with high CTR. The homepage ranks around 32 and does little. - Queries are very specific: named entities (buyers, companies), classification codes and place names. Rivals cover these thinly. - Near page one: code explainers ("cpv code ...") and region hubs ("ausschreibungen city"). Hub pages look like the next lever. - Some impressions come from machine-generated queries (long chains of -site: filters). They are worth little, so do not count them as demand. - The last weekly bucket is probably reporting lag, not a drop. ## What to do differently (hypotheses) - Prefer ideas built on **open, regularly updated public data** that yields many distinct, useful pages people search for by name or code, especially in German or other non-English markets. - Each page must carry real data (no thin pages or doorway pages). - Be more cautious with single-job English SaaS tools: we have no traction data for that kind yet. - Do not trust a composite rated by one agent alone. Wait for the blind reviewers.
learning.calibration: The ratings cannot be trusted or distrusted yet: there are zero projects with outcomes, and the only idea was rated by the Scout alone. The single site with traction is an owner site the agents never rated, so it says nothing about how accurate the ratings are.

proposedFactors.description: The product exposes an MCP server, a small command line tool, an llms.txt file or a skill listing, so AI agents can call it and become a source of users.
A memorable change to an existing platform's URL turns any of its links into the product's result page, which brings direct traffic without search.
Free self-hostable open source wins GitHub and community reach, while a paid hosted version earns from users who do not want to run servers.
Growth came mainly from the founder's existing following, so the case should be weighted lower as evidence that the product itself works.
